title: The Valentine's Doggy Date
clue: Four tiny tables, no reservations and a very good guest.
reveal: Set four low 'tables' for a quiet date. Each offers a different kind of attention: play, sniffing, closeness and calm company. Your dog wanders between them and the one they return to most becomes the main event.
objective: Let your dog visit four tables of attention and spend ten minutes at the one they choose.
instructions: Clear a corner and keep chocolate, candy hearts, sweets with xylitol, roses, lilies, candles, balloons and ribbon well away. Lay four mats or towels a few steps apart.
Make each table different: Play (a favorite toy), Sniff (a clean worn T-shirt of yours and a clean cloth of theirs), Close (a cushion beside your chair), Calm (a blanket with you reading nearby).
Sit out of the way and let your dog wander. They may visit tables in any order and as often as they like, or none.
After a few minutes, notice which table they return to most. If they ignore them all, follow what they do instead.
Spend ten minutes at the favorite table: play, sniff, sit close or share the quiet. Let them lead the intensity.
Close the date quietly, give fresh water and let them rest.
twist: The date has four kinds of attention and your dog orders by wandering, so you see which one they ask for.
variations: Food-free by design; no treats needed.
Outdoor date: put the tables on a blanket in a yard or park.
For a shy dog: use two tables only.
For a puppy: three minutes of each, then a nap.
completion: Your dog has visited the tables and you have spent time at the favorite.
photoIdea: A quiet shot of your dog at the table they chose, close but not posed.
memoryPrompt: Which table did your dog choose?
safety: Chocolate, candy hearts and xylitol sweets are dangerous; keep all sweets and flowers out of reach.
No candles, balloons or ribbon in the room, and no wine glasses.
Let your dog leave any table or the whole date at any time.
